title: Chapter 1870: Broadjade (II)
content:
Chapter 1870: Broadjade (II)

Li Ximing glanced over the mountain, stirred by a thought. Silently connecting to the Immortal Artifact, he unleashed his ability to search the unseen. His view immediately cleared, revealing the mountain's wood-grained surface.

Yet beneath the mist, bones lay piled across the mountains, and dead trees had collapsed everywhere. Not a single patch was clean. Rivers of blood surged as though breathing, nourishing clouds and rain wreathed in spiritual energy.

A sea of devil cultivators indeed. This truly is a blood-soaked shore... They merely use [Gathering Wood] to concentrate blood essence and nourish spirit materials.

He surveyed it without betraying his surprise. Baoxiang, meanwhile, recalled something and smiled. "It does have its benefits... Since this qi obscures spiritual sense, quite a few children of destiny have risen to prominence here. Thirty percent of the Western Sea's Purple Mansion Realm cultivators came from [Lesser Broadjade Mountain]!"

Li Ximing’s gaze swept across the mountain. Through the Immortal Artifact, he discovered faint traces of reflected palaces on the still sea at the mountain's foot. They were enormous, seemingly built for something other than humans.

The palaces were ancient and roughly hewn, but lay in ruins, their broken forms indistinct amid varying shades of green. Huge statues had toppled on either side. He could faintly make out shattered scales and enormous serpentine bodies carved from stone.

His heart stirred. Recalling what he had heard about the Western Sea, he asked, "I've heard there is also a [Greater Broadjade Mountain]..."

Baoxiang noticed nothing amiss and explained seriously, "

Ah.

[Greater Broadjade Mountain] lies far away on the seabed. It was once the Western Sea Dragon King's palace and is now the residence of a great figure, so we generally avoid speaking of it. Another place is more intriguing. People of the Western Sea call it [Middle Broadjade Mountain]. It lies neither above the sea nor beneath it."

Li Ximing smiled, deliberately asking a question whose answer he already suspected. "

Oh?

Since it belongs to Mansion Water, it cannot stand in the sky either. Is it in the great void, then?"

Riding her Pit Water, the woman replied, "It is within the reflection on the water."

She continued, "It was once the palace of Dongfang Fengchi, the sixth young master of the True Hornless Dragon. As he held a [Pristine Water] position, he drew upon the imagery of Gathering Wood establishing Mansion Water to create a pool that was as still as a mirror. It lies within the reflection of [Lesser Broadjade Mountain], and is what we call [Middle Broadjade Mountain].

"Later, the Western Sea Dragon King Dongfang Yuezhu joined forces with the other dragons to eliminate him, leaving the place deserted. Occasionally, when the wind and rain cease and the clear and turbid waters separate, the ruins of [Middle Broadjade Mountain] can still be seen in the reflection."

Li Ximing murmured his wonder. The Immortal Artifact had already revealed it clearly, so the ruins had to be that former demon palace. Secretly urging its mystics onward, he found nothing but ruins within. At the highest point stood a throne as large as a palace, split in two. Everything lay in disarray, empty and devoid of treasures.

He asked in surprise, "Wouldn't that make it a grotto heaven? Has any Daoist tried entering it?"

Baoxiang visibly paused, clearly not expecting him to make the connection so quickly. She sank into thought. "Well..."

Before Baoxiang could answer, Li Ximing's searching gaze came to a halt. A horrifying sight had appeared before him. Amid the reflection of those endless ancient ruins, a speck of green stirred.

It was a figure in green robes. Dressed in green with golden tassels, the man lounged against an enormous step as high as a seat. His face was sinister and uncanny, his eyes long and narrow like a serpent's. Green-black hair hung loose, dark and frightening.

He gazed upward, holding a green apricot with a bite already taken from it. The fruit swayed gently as his fingers moved, and an amused expression played across his face.

A chill shot through Li Ximing with terrifying speed, filling his throat and mind.

That face was all too familiar.

Suiguan.

The Grand Daoist Master who had emerged from Pristine Cadence Heaven. The Purple Mansion Realm cultivator suspected of being a manifestation of the mystics of Du Qing, True Monarch of Pristine Water. The fiend who had personally brought about the slaughter of a million through turbid killing!

He's looking at me.

To Li Ximing, this ghostlike Grand Daoist Master with perfected divine abilities was no different from Du Qing's own eyes! His appearance on the northern shore years ago had been frightening enough. Now he had abruptly appeared within Li Ximing’s ability to search the unseen!

Has he been hiding here all along? Or...

He dared not betray the slightest reaction or deliberately avert his eyes. He continued gazing at the sea as though admiring the view.

The Grand Daoist Master moved. Suiguan held the green apricot between his lips, freeing both hands. His smile seemed to fade as he sat a little straighter, still staring at Li Ximing's face.

The suffocating moment lasted two full breaths before Baoxiang chuckled. "They wouldn't dare... They're all afraid that what they step into won't be [Middle Broadjade Mountain], but Pristine Cadence Heaven!"

They ought to be afraid...

Her words were a lifeline. Li Ximing turned toward her with a look of surprise, still smiling. He shook out his sleeves and tucked his hands behind his back. "Surely you jest! Pristine Cadence Heaven is far away in Jiangnan!"

In that brief moment where he turned toward the Daoist Master beside him, he severed his connection to the Immortal Artifact. Yet its mystics were so extraordinary that, even as he turned, he caught one last glimpse of the scene below.

The ruined steps were empty.

The green-robed man now stood at the very top of the reflection, his robes billowing and his arms folded across his chest. The green apricot was now in his pale hand. That sinister face was only a fist's breadth from breaking through the surface. Li Ximing needed only to lift his eyes to see him.

Eyes woven with green and purple light watched him quietly, with a trace of amusement.

The seawater was so clear it might as well not have been there.
